Karen — thanks, and appreciate the clarity. Quick response with a proposed approach so you can share with Marco/security: 

1) Evidence binder (staged): we can deliver a "staged evidence binder" on a timed schedule. Contents: nightly snapshot archives (logical), signed runbook excerpts for operator procedures, access logs for the proposed audit window, and a redacted operator credential roll history. Proposed initial delivery: 10 business days after order form countersigned.

2) Operator key custody: Redwood prefers a third-party custodian for custodial escrow of long-term operator keys. For short-term investigative access we can provide a time-limited console session (SAML-issued) accompanied by an on-record attestation signed by our Head of Ops. We will propose MSA language that: (a) limits operator key use to defined audit windows; (b) requires Redwood to record and provide audit logs for any session; and (c) permits MediSys to witness key material retrieval via an independent custodian.

3) Audit window & verification: propose two standard options — (A) one-week rolling audit window per quarter or (B) a single four-hour onsite virtual verification. We can support both; pick one and we'll tailor the runbook.

I've attached a working doc with the staged binder outline and proposed timeline. Rishi — can you add a short diagram of the snapshot flow so they can see what we mean by "logical snapshot"? Aditya — flag any legal redlines you see inline and I'll coordinate with Marco.

Karen / Naomi — adding the technical constraints so expectations are aligned. Short version:

- "Snapshot" here is a logical, application-level snapshot (model weights + serving config + minimal runtime state) that we can export as a signed artifact. It is not a raw disk image.
- Delivery: snapshots will be delivered via encrypted transfer to a customer-controlled S3 bucket or via a 3rd-party custody exchange (we usually use Custodia Partners). Each snapshot includes a SHA256 digest and our operator signature.
- Attestation: we can provide a signed attestation that includes the operator account identity, approximate timestamp (UTC), and a short statement of the actions taken. Attestation can be issued by Redwood's Head of Platform.
- Key Rotation: we support scheduled rotation; if MediSys requires on-demand rotation tied to an audit, we can coordinate a joint rotation with the custodian.

I've attached a simple diagram of the delivery flow and the minimal metadata we include. If MediSys needs HSM-backed export instead of the custodian flow, call that out and we'll escalate to engineering for feasibility and lead time.

Attachments: [Attachment: snapshot-process-diagram.png (120KB, PNG)]

Thanks,

Naomi / team — thanks for the quick notes. Attached are marked redlines to the proposed MSA addendum. Key open points we need Redwood to confirm or revise: 

- Replace "third-party custodian (recommended)" with explicit language that names acceptable custodians or allows customer approval of the custodian.

- Forensics access: we want a firm audit window (date range) rather than a rolling "one-week per quarter" unless Redwood can guarantee specific snapshot retention.
- Evidence binder contents: ask Redwood to commit to a checklist in the addendum (we provided a suggested checklist on p.3 of the redlines).
